written_before: arm B's launch — this file is committed BEFORE tools/atlas/steered_frontier.py is invoked for arm B, and arm A was already COMPLETE and on record when it was written. The windows below are therefore pre-registered against arm B and post-hoc against arm A; arm A's numbers were read once (see `arm_a_anchors`) and are frozen here so a later read cannot move them.
question: Over one unattended night at a fixed wall budget, does the harvest-v2 pop-quota allocator (deficit-derived quotas + a universal 5% floor) admit more distinct-q3 locations than the deficit scheduler?

A.status: COMPLETE (stopped on its own wall cap at 519.86 of 520 min)

B.status: to be launched immediately after this file is committed

matched_on: code: both launched from the steered_frontier at ba7e284's content EXCEPT the root-draw budget (see known_confounds)
julia supply pool: data/atlas/julia_supply_pool_v3.json (209 c, min |dc| 3.20e-2), resolved by default in both
differs_by_construction: --pop-quota instead of --scheduler (mutually exclusive; both name the pop). This IS the treatment.

the library look seed: --pop-quota denominates demand in HUMAN LABELS, so it never attempts the seed and stamps library_seed.status=never_attempted. Arm A stamped status=seeded (168 looks in the artifact / 154 after the medoid dedup). This is not a separable nuisance — it is part of what the allocator IS.
primary_estimand: cumulative admissions (totals.admitted = distinct q3) at each arm's own 520-minute WALL cap.

matched_wall.point: each arm's own wall cap, 520 min (arm A landed at 519.86)
matched_wall.why_terminal_only: cumulative WALL is not reconstructible at intermediate points for arm A: the per-batch run.log line stamps per-batch seconds and CUMULATIVE ACTIVE minutes only (their sum, 453.3 m, reproduces active_min 453.58, not wall_min 519.86), and the ledger's `ts` field carries the run id, not a timestamp. The 15% wall-over-active gap is in-loop root replenishment, which is unstamped. So the only honest matched-wall point is the shared terminal cap.
matched_wall.contingency: if arm B stops on something other than its wall cap (active cap, STOP sentinel, crash), the matched-wall read is VOID as a matched read: report both arms at their own stop with the wall gap named, and let the matched-batch and late-marginal windows carry the comparison. Do not rescale.

matched_batch.terminal: B_star = min(last batch index in each arm's harvest_log.jsonl)
matched_batch.note: index 137 is where the 59.5-minute proving run stopped; it is kept only so the earlier 2.6x reading is legible on the same axis, NOT because it is a fair comparison point.

late_marginal.batch_window: the last 300 batches of [1, B_star] — i.e. batches (B_star-300, B_star]
late_marginal.why: arm A's rate ROSE monotonically all night (0.49/active-min at b328 to 0.74 cumulative, ~0.86 marginal late). A cumulative average therefore compares two different mixtures of cold and warm frontier; the marginal window is the one that answers 'which allocator is better once both frontiers have built'.
late_marginal.instrument_note: the per-batch ACTIVE clock comes from each run's run.log (gitignored, present on disk). If a run.log is missing the active-normalized figures are reported UNKNOWN — never omitted, never back-filled from the mean batch cost, which would assume a uniform per-batch cost the run visibly does not have.

decision_rule.adopt_pop_quota_as_default_allocator_iff: arm B beats arm A by >= +10% relative on BOTH the primary (matched-wall cumulative admissions) AND the late-marginal window (admissions per active-min over the last 300 batches).
decision_rule.keep_scheduler_iff: arm A beats arm B by >= +10% relative on both.
decision_rule.otherwise: REPORT DISAGREE and adopt neither. Two reads that can fail in opposite directions are the point: a cumulative win with a marginal loss means the winner front-loaded, and one night of each is not enough to spend that.
decision_rule.margin_basis: 10% is a tolerance, not a knee. Arm A's own late-vs-cumulative spread is 0.86 vs 0.74 (16%), so a gap under 10% is inside the variation one run shows against itself across its own night.

known_confounds: ROOT-DRAW BUDGET: arm A launched before ROOT_DRAW_BUDGET_S was raised 25 -> 40 min (commits 468127b/16cc9e9, after arm A started). Arm B carries 40. The bound is a hang backstop OUTSIDE both caps and did not bind in arm A (pre-loop draw took 9.17 min against it), so it cannot move either arm's in-cap yield — but 'same code' is not literally true and this is the difference.

VARIETY IS NOT COMPARABLE. Arm A reports 309 distinct looks; a --pop-quota run has no scheduler and stamps totals.distinct_looks = 0 (the proving run did). The comparison is therefore denominated in ADMISSIONS, not in distinct looks, which is the denomination the discovery pipeline actually prefers. Reading a variety difference off this pair requires a post-hoc embed pass over both ledgers that is NOT part of this pre-registration.

BOX CONTENTION. Arm A ran overnight on an otherwise quiet box. Arm B launches during a labeling session on the same box. Labeling is GPU-light and engine-free, but this is not a matched condition and it can only hurt arm B.
SINGLE RUN PER ARM. No seed replication. A 10% margin on n=1 per arm is a tolerance for reading the direction, not a confidence interval.

The 59.5-minute proving run (harvest_v2_proving_20260803) is BACKGROUND ONLY — different code era, julia_supply_pool_v2, and it stopped inside the cold phase arm A crossed at 0.19 admissions/min. It is not a third arm.
